title: 132 Pattern
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of `n` integers. A **132 pattern** is a triple of indices `i < j < k` such that `nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j]`: the value at the first index is the smallest, the value at the middle index is the largest, and the value at the last index lies strictly between the other two.

Determine whether `nums` contains at least one 132 pattern. Print `true` if it does and `false` otherwise.

The three values must be strictly ordered, so equal values never form a pattern on their own.

**Follow-up:** be ready to explain the approaches from the brute force to the optimal one, and to dry-run your solution on an example.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.

examples.explanation: Take indices 1, 2, 3: the values are 1, 4, 2 and 1 < 2 < 4, so this is a 132 pattern.
The array is strictly decreasing, so for any i < k we have nums[i] > nums[k]. No triple can satisfy nums[i] < nums[k].
Indices 0, 1, 3 give the values 2, 8, 5 and 2 < 5 < 8. Repeated values such as the two 5s do not matter as long as one valid triple exists.

hints: Brute force tries every triple in O(n^3). Fix the middle index j and note that the best choice for i is the smallest value to its left; that already gives O(n^2).
Scan from right to left and think of the pair (j, k): you want the largest possible value for nums[k] that is still smaller than some nums[j] to its left.

Maintain a monotonic decreasing stack of candidate 'j' values and a variable `third` holding the largest value ever popped (a valid nums[k]). If the current element is smaller than `third`, you have found nums[i].
